props.heading: Define your schema.
props.description: Tessera turns a typed schema into a database, API, auth, and realtime. No glue code, no drift.

props.heading: One schema, four steps to a live backend
props.description: Define it once. Tessera builds the database, the API, and the types, and keeps them in sync while you ship.

steps.title: Schema
steps.description: Define tables, relations, and rules in TypeScript. One schema powers your database, API, and types.

steps.title: Data
steps.description: Push, and Tessera plans a safe migration from the diff. Every branch gets its own copy of the data.

steps.title: Query
steps.description: Query with a typed builder. Change a column and the compiler shows you what breaks.

steps.title: Live
steps.description: Subscribe to any query. Presence and broadcast are built in, with no sockets to manage.

props.heading:
Trusted by teams
shipping real products
props.description: From fintech dashboards to one-person SaaS, teams build their backends on Tessera. Hear from a few of them.

items.title: Northwind Labs
items.quote: “We deleted about 6,000 lines of glue code the week we moved to Tessera. Backend setup went from three weeks to two days, and features ship three times faster because the types follow the schema.”
items.name: Priya Raman

items.title: Loop & Co.
items.quote: “Preview environments per pull request changed how we review backend work. We shipped realtime editing without running a socket layer, and median sync sits at 40 ms.”
items.name: Marcus Lee

items.title: fieldnote
items.quote: “Types that go from the database all the way to the component. That alone sold us. One developer, one schema, twelve thousand users, and a first-year infra bill of zero.”
items.name: Jonas Berg
Maya Chen
items.quote: Wrote a schema, ran tessera push, and had a typed API before my coffee cooled. @tessera is kind of unfair.

items.name: David Okafor
items.quote: Database branches per PR is the feature I didn’t know I needed. Reviewing migrations is boring now, in a good way.

items.name: Jin Park
items.quote: Renamed a column and the compiler pointed at all 14 places that broke. That’s the whole pitch for @tessera.

items.name: Lin Zhou
items.quote: Moved our realtime feed off a hand-rolled socket server. Deleted about 2k lines and nobody noticed except the on-call rotation.

items.name: Sam Ortiz
items.quote: The generated Python client matches the TypeScript one exactly. Our data team stopped asking me for endpoints.

items.name: Ada Novak
items.quote: Row-level rules right next to the table definition. Why wasn’t it always like this?

items.name: Nora Eriksen
items.quote: The @tessera migration planner caught a destructive change I would have shipped on a Friday.

items.name: Kwame Mensah
items.quote: 38 ms median for subscriptions from Frankfurt. I checked twice.

props.heading:
Four building blocks.
One source of truth.
props.description: Database, auth, realtime, and functions share a single schema, so they never disagree.

items.title: Database
items.description: Postgres, with types that follow you. Every branch gets its own copy of the data.

items.title: Auth
items.description: Email, OAuth, or magic links, with access rules next to the data they protect.

items.title: Realtime
items.description: Every query can be a subscription, with presence and broadcast built in.

items.title: Functions
items.description: Server code without the servers. Attach a trigger and it runs close to your data.
